output.brief:
The rise to 0.41% is most likely ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354% with a normal upper edge of 0.482%. Three earlier weeks went higher (0.44, 0.47, 0.51), and the investigations of those found nothing. The dashboard counts match raw log counts, so this is not a counting artefact. The burn-rate page did not fire (0.82x against a 2x threshold). Customers were not visibly affected: bookings were flat, no complaints came in, and retries recovered about 98.6% of failed requests.

The finding that new pods error at nearly twice the rate of old ones is a rollout warm-up effect. It appears in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy of unchanged code. New pods start with empty caches and time out against the database. That adds only 10–20 errors per rollout. It does not show that v4.18 is faulty.

I can't rule out the replica host move or partner-sync month-end load as small contributors. Neither is needed to explain the week.

Next steps:
- Don't roll back.
- Don't mute alerting. Muting the burn-rate page would remove a protective control.
- Note the week at ops review and apply the standard check to the following week.
- If next week exceeds the band, investigate then.
- Consider cache pre-warming for rollouts.
